baseline.changes_summary: async-fifo-queue.ts is unchanged. lock-manager.ts: telemetry (trace/span) removed from extendLocks; cancelJob, cancelAllJobs, getActiveJobCount, isRunning, getTrackedJobIds dropped. worker.ts: excerpt of run, mainLoop, _getNextJob, processJob, getUnrecoverableErrorMessage, handleCompleted, handleFailed and their helpers; telemetry removed (trace/span, which de-indents processJob); extends EventEmitter instead of QueueBase; short constructor with the original defaults; Redis calls replaced by the QueueBackend stub; moveToActive/nextJobFromJobData simplified to take a Job instead of raw job data; retryIfFailed simplified to retry connection errors once; close(), pause/resume, the stalled checker, sandboxing and job schedulers dropped. types.ts is new: stand-ins for Job, Processor, WorkerOptions (doc comments copied from BullMQ), QueueBackend, LockManagerWorkerContext, error classes, delay.

review.notes: Built by Claude from internal/build-instructions.md; not yet reviewed. For the reviewer: (1) Length is 980 lines (worker 470, lock-manager 153, async-fifo-queue 196, types 161), over the 500-650 target; the rest is BullMQ's four-parameter generics and helpers mainLoop needs to compile. Dropping the generics would save ~60 lines but changes the original code. (2) close() was dropped for length, so graceful-shutdown is no longer in `present`. (3) Compile settings are BullMQ's own (strict, but strictNullChecks off), not plain --strict: async-fifo-queue.ts does not compile under strictNullChecks. (4) Q5 names untrackJob and Q8 says 'long-running': both point toward the bug. (5) The lockDuration doc comment in types.ts (copied from BullMQ) explains what happens when a lock is lost: the main clue, kept on purpose. (6) Licence checked by Claude from LICENSE and package.json at the commit; needs a human check.
